subtopics.title: The Cosine Rule and Where It Comes From

questions.question: In a² = b² + c² − 2bc·cos A, the side a and the angle A must:
options: Face each other across the triangle
Both be the largest in the triangle

questions.question: In the proof, the two b² terms merge because:
Setting A = 90° in the cosine rule gives:
options: a² = b² + c² — Pythagoras, since cos 90° = 0 kills the correction term

questions.question: The proof begins by:
options: Dropping a perpendicular from C onto AB, creating right-angled triangles

subtopics.title: Finding a Side — Two Sides and the Included Angle

questions.question: With b = 8, c = 3 and A = 60°, side a equals:
With p = 7, r = 8 and included angle Q = 120°, the correction term −2(7)(8)cos 120° becomes:
options: PLUS 56, because cos 120° = −0,5 and two minuses make a plus

questions.question: That obtuse case gives q² = 113 + 56 = 169, so q equals:
If an obtuse-angle answer comes out SHORTER than the right-angle (Pythagoras) value, it means:
options: A minus sign was fumbled — an angle beyond 90° must push the far side longer
The sine rule should have been used

subtopics.title: Finding an Angle — Three Sides, No Angle

questions.question: In cos A = (b² + c² − a²)/(2bc), the side subtracted on top is:
options: Either of the sides next to A
The side OPPOSITE the angle being hunted

questions.question: For sides 4, 7 and 9, the largest angle is found opposite:
options: The side of 9, since the largest angle faces the longest side
Any side — the choice is free

questions.question: The calculation gives cos θ = −16/56 = −0,2857, so θ is:
options: 106,6° — the negative cosine announced an obtuse angle
Impossible, since cosine cannot be negative

questions.question: Unlike inverse sine, inverse cosine has no 'second suspect' at 180° − θ because:
options: cos(180° − θ) has the OPPOSITE sign, not the same value
Inverse cosine only outputs acute angles

subtopics.title: Two-Dimensional Problems — Harbours, Bearings and Shared Sides

questions.question: Boats on bearings 040° and 105° from the same harbour enclose an angle of:
With HP = 5 km, HQ = 7 km and angle PHQ = 65°, the distance PQ is:
The angle at P was found with the cosine rule rather than the sine rule because:
options: The sine rule cannot find angles
The angle might have been obtuse, and inverse cosine settles acute-versus-obtuse on its own
The cosine rule is always shorter
No sides were known in the triangle

questions.question: In every 2D story problem, the first physical action should be:
options: Translating the words into a labelled sketch

questions.question: In the two-paths picture, a corner WIDER than 90° means the friends finish:
options: Further apart than Pythagoras predicts — the correction adds

questions.question: For paths of 7 m and 8 m with a 120° corner, the separation is:
At exactly 90°, the correction term disappears because:
options: cos 90° = 0, and the rule becomes ordinary Pythagoras
The triangle collapses to a line

questions.question: The recommended calculator habit for the cosine rule is:
options: Compute the correction term separately and subtract by hand
Round cos of the angle to one decimal first
Type the whole right-hand side in one line, cosine in brackets, and press equals once

questions.question: Holding two sides and the angle pinched between them (Side-Angle-Side) calls for:
options: The cosine rule — the sine rule stalls with no complete opposite pair

questions.question: Holding a side together with its opposite angle — a complete pair — means:
options: The sine rule is available, and being lighter, it should carry the next step
Only the cosine rule may be used
The area rule must come first

questions.question: Inverse sine is 'the witness who cannot tell twins apart' because:
options: An acute angle and its 180°-minus partner have identical sines

questions.question: Writing the stocktake sentence — 'two sides and the included angle are known, so the cosine rule applies' — is worth doing because:
options: It replaces the need for a sketch
It doubles the final answer's accuracy
It earns the method mark and stops the wrong formula before it starts

questions.question: In every two-triangle story, the two triangles are connected by:
options: Exactly one shared side — the bridge
A shared angle at the top

questions.question: The correct order of work is:
options: Solve the triangle whose stocktake is complete, extract the bridge, then cross into the second
Always begin with the triangle containing the final answer
Guess the bridge and verify at the end

questions.question: Crossing the bridge with the rounded 6,66 instead of the full calculator value causes:
options: No effect, since rounding is always safe
The second triangle to become obtuse
A seeded error that grows through the second triangle and costs accuracy marks

questions.question: Before computing anything in a two-triangle question, you should:
options: Erase the given diagram and redraw it larger
Circle the shared side and note which triangle supplies it and which spends it
